title: Do stubborn walkers who convert after meeting robots let a smaller robot minority tip a crowd's walking side?
summary: The society-converts model with 40% stubborn walkers who each convert to an ordinary memory-rule walker after meeting a committed robot k times, instead of at a constant rate. With the block fixed, 28% robots tip 5 of 12 simulated crowds; with exposure conversion at k = 30 every crowd at 24% robots tips (median round 171, 12 of 12) and every stubborn walker has converted by round 1000 at every robot share tried, yet 16% and 20% robots still never tip: the threshold falls to the no-block value, not below it. Tipping time follows the conversion time (about k/ρ rounds). An exposure-blind rate with the same mean time to convert (ρ/k) tips at the same robot shares but up to 1.8 times sooner at larger k (but later at k = 1 and 3) (median round 62 against 110 at 28% robots, k = 30), because it converts a few people from round one. Stylised: well-mixed meetings, no geometry, 200 people, 12 seeds; robot share is the only exposure source.
lede: do stubborn walkers who convert after meeting robots let a smaller robot minority tip a crowd's walking side? At 24% robots every crowd tips for k = 30 meetings (median round 171) though the fixed block stops it; at 16-20% none tip.
